historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(ci): build gomod2nix from repo flake so it uses the pinned Go
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The update-gomod2nix workflow installed gomod2nix via
`nix profile install github:nix-community/gomod2nix`, which builds it
against upstream gomod2nix's own stale nixpkgs (an older Go) with
GOTOOLCHAIN=local. That Go — not the one on PATH — runs `go mod
download`, so it failed with `go.mod requires go >= 1.26.1 (running go
1.24.5)`.

Install from the repo's own dev/nix flake instead. Its overlay builds
gomod2nix against the Go version pinned in dev/nix/conf.nix (single
source of truth, kept in sync with go.mod). Export gomod2nix from the
flake's packages, bump the flake.lock nixpkgs so go_1_26 (>=1.26.1) is
available, and drop the now-redundant setup-go step.

Signed-off-by: Alan Clucas <alan@clucas.org>

historicalFixesSummary.body:
The configmap sync endpoints relied solely on the kube client's identity
for RBAC, which is only effective in Client auth mode. In Server or SSO
(without RBAC) modes, the server's own privileged kube client is used,
bypassing authorization entirely. Add explicit SelfSubjectAccessReview
checks for configmap permissions before each operation, matching the
pattern used by the database sync provider.

Fixes a security issue introduced in #14724.

Signed-off-by: Alan Clucas <alan@clucas.org>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

historicalFixesSummary.body:
Use strings.Cut instead of strings.Split to safely parse the
pod-gc-strategy annotation. The unchecked parts[1] access
caused an index-out-of-bounds panic when the annotation value
contained no "/" separator, crashing the controller process
via the informer goroutine which runs outside the recover scope.
